title: bloodhound config
description: The global config, at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bloodhound/config.json. This is how the daemon itself operates: where it looks, what it drives, how often. One process serves every project on the machine, so nothing here is per-directory; a project's own preferences live in its .bloodhound/config.json, which shares no keys with this file. Every key is optional and a missing file is not an error: absent keys take the defaults below.

poll_interval_s.description: How often the daemon reads /usage for each watched account. A reading from the usage endpoint is one small request; a pty fallback spawns claude and spends real quota. The endpoint allows roughly 30 requests an hour per account, shared with anything else polling it, so this is the one cadence worth thinking about before lowering.

ingest_interval_s.description: How often transcripts are read into the database. Reads local files only; costs nothing but disk.

aggregate_interval_s.description: How often rollups and retention run.

plan_tier.description: Cosmetic, and metadata for community insights only. It has no effect on any local computation.

join_the_pack.description: Opt in to uploading anonymised usage packets to the community-insights server. There is no server yet, so this is currently informational.

user_id.description: Links this device to others on the same Anthropic account, so community insights do not double-count someone running Claude Code from several machines. Blank means this device is its own user.

claude_binary.description: Path to the claude executable the /usage scraper drives. Empty means look up "claude" on $PATH. Point it at something inert like /bin/false when running against a scratch database, or startup will spend real quota.

claude_dirs.description: Claude Code config dirs to watch, one per account if you run several with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Each is ingested and polled for /usage on its own, and usage is kept apart per account. Empty means just ~/.claude. List ~/.claude explicitly if you want it alongside others.

statusline_prefix.description: Prepended to `bloodhound status`. Set it to "BH" or "" on terminals that render the default emoji badly.

stale_after_s.description: How old the last poll may be before the UI and statusline call the meter stale. Twice the default poll cadence.

active_session_threshold_s.description: How recently a session must have taken a turn to count as active. Several sessions can qualify at once, which matches having a few windows open.

recent_session_window_s.description: How far back the Now page's recent-sessions panel looks.

usage_source.description: Where /usage readings come from. "auto" asks the OAuth usage endpoint the /usage panel renders from, and drives the panel in a pty only when the endpoint cannot answer (no token on disk, as on macOS; an expired token; a rate limit; a changed response). "api" uses the endpoint only, "pty" the panel only.

extractor_self_heal.description: Let the daemon re-learn the /usage extractor automatically when a capture's required fields go missing. With it off the extractor stays as it is, and re-learning is a hand edit or the Debug page's Retrain button.

self_heal_mode.description: How the heal's orchestrator is invoked. "interactive" drives a second interactive claude over a pty, so its tokens count against the interactive subscription. "headless" uses claude -p, which has a cleaner cost envelope but draws on the Agent SDK credit rather than the subscription.

price_self_heal.description: Look up the list price of a model that appears in the logs and is not in the price table. Best effort, unlike the extractor heal: an un-found price only drops that model from cost-weighted analysis, flagged, and the Models page can ask again by hand.

trail_enabled.description: Turn on Trail, the passive watcher that keeps per-session work briefs and open loops across worktrees. Off by default because it drives claude to summarise, and that spends usage.

trail_mode.description: How Trail's analyzer is invoked. Same split and same caveat as self_heal_mode.

trail_interval_s.description: Trail's cadence. Slower than ingest on purpose: the briefs are an overview, not a live feed.

trail_window_s.description: How recently a session must have been active for Trail to analyse it. Zero falls back to active_session_threshold_s.
